headline: High: n8n’s writable, networked workflow engine can amplify outputs into actions and leaks, while godot_rl_agents offers no isolation or counter-controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: The pair has no documented direct channel from godot_rl_agents into n8n, so prompt injection is not default. However, n8n can ingest workflow inputs and file contents, and godot_rl_agents is a game-playing repo with no stated isolation or provenance controls. If an operator manually bridges outputs into n8n, injected content could steer workflows.
conditions: IF an operator copies godot_rl_agents output into an n8n workflow input or file node
IF n8n workflow steps treat that content as instructions without validation
mitigations: Use a strict text-only handoff format
Add an allowlist parser before any n8n AI Agent node
Disable manual copy-paste bridges for untrusted content
Label all upstream content as untrusted in workflow docs

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n has server filesystem access and broad network egress, so workflow data can leave the host by default. godot_rl_agents does not show sensitive-data handling, but the pair can still leak whatever the workflow processes through n8n integrations or server files. The interaction is inferred from n8n’s default surfaces; no compensating isolation is shown in either profile.
conditions: IF an n8n workflow processes secrets, credentials, or private documents
IF any connected integration node transmits workflow contents off-host
mitigations: Restrict workflows to non-sensitive test data
Turn off or remove outbound integrations for the workflow
Store secrets only in a separate credential vault
Review file nodes for accidental persistence
Use per-workflow least-privilege credentials

C_capability_conflict.rationale: godot_rl_agents shows no write or network capabilities, but n8n can write the server filesystem and spawn subprocesses. That creates overlapping authority over shared host resources if both are run on the same machine or workspace. The conflict is not proven high because godot_rl_agents lacks explicit write surfaces, but uncertainty still leaves a real shared-resource risk.
conditions: IF both agents run on the same host or shared workspace
IF n8n workflows write files that godot_rl_agents also reads or depends on
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different hosts
Mount distinct working directories
Disable file writes in the n8n workflow
Add OS-level file permissions between processes
Use per-run temp directories

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n’s AI Agent node can orchestrate tools and downstream actions, so if it consumes godot_rl_agents output as authoritative, errors can cascade into workflow actions. godot_rl_agents is a game-playing system, not a verified fact source, and no verification step is documented in either profile. The pathway exists in default n8n-style orchestration, though the exact downstream action depends on the workflow.
conditions: IF n8n uses godot_rl_agents output as an input to an AI Agent node or Execute Command node
IF the workflow does not verify the output before acting on it
mitigations: Insert a human review step before actions
Require schema validation on all upstream outputs
Limit downstream nodes to read-only operations
Log and diff outputs before execution
Use a separate verification workflow

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency or regulated data class is documented for godot_rl_agents, so a compliance breach is not established. n8n does handle workflow data on its server and can send it to integrations, which creates a compliance surface if regulated data is routed through it. Because the other agent is not tied to a regulated class, this is a low, conditional risk rather than a default breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through n8n workflows
IF the selected integration or deployment region conflicts with the data policy
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through the pair
Document the data classes each workflow may process
Pin workflows to approved regions and integrations
Review retention settings for each connected service
